You are a senior full-stack engineer + data-viz designer on a hackathon team (demo today 14:00, hand-in 12:00). Build the LAUNCH TIMELINE, the new central visual of the product, plus the small backend data it needs. Work in the repo directly; do NOT commit or push. Another engineer rebuilds the app shell in parallel: you may ONLY edit web/src/components/LaunchTimeline.tsx (currently a placeholder with the agreed props interface; keep `export function LaunchTimeline(props: LaunchTimelineProps)` and the props exactly: {state, nowMs, selectedId, onSelect, compact?}), web/src/lib/api.ts (add types only; do not change existing exports' behaviour), src/ask_soony/api.py (build_state / build_strip and helpers they need), src/ask_soony/launch.py if needed, and tests/ (new test file). Do not touch App.tsx, Rail.tsx, DecisionCard.tsx, StatusStrip.tsx, EvidenceDrawer.tsx, Routines*, routines/*.

Repo /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony. Read docs/challenge.md (packing windows Sat 06:00-22:00 and Sun 06:00-20:00 local Europe/Berlin, no night shift; trucks leave Sun 22 Nov 20:00; Standard 3 lines ~6,100/h, 9 h slack at kickoff; Collector's 1 manual cell 900/h, 2 h slack, "every hour the cell waits costs 900 copies"). Read src/ask_soony/launch.py (PackClock), src/ask_soony/api.py build_state/build_strip/build_cards, web/src/lib/api.ts (State, StripItem, Card, Shipment). Live server on :8000 from this checkout (login form /login, password ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in .env, never print it); it does NOT auto-reload Python: to test backend changes run a second server, e.g. `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD=... uv run uvicorn ask_soony.api:app --port 8012` without ASK_BACKGROUND (stop it when done).

Design (agreed by three design reviews):
1. Backend: add `clock` to /api/state: {launch: ISO (Sun 20:00 local), windows: [[start,end],...] shift windows from now's day to launch (from PackClock if available, else the brief's defaults), editions: [{edition, label, finishes_at: ISO|null, stops_at: ISO|null, copies_at_risk, slack_hours}]}. Also make the numbers CONSISTENT with the open cards: today the strip says "Standard 32,000 at risk" while cards say 20,000 and 34,800, and "Collector's on track · 0 at risk" while red cards exist for Collector's parts (art books ~5,900 short, statues ~3,400 short; see findings/impacts in data/state written by scripts/demo_cards.py: check their `edition` values and fix the mapping if a card's impact edition does not match the strip's edition keys, e.g. FG-GH6-STD / FG-GH6-CE or labels). Never invent numbers: derive per-edition copies at risk from the open cards' impacts/numbers for that edition (max or a clearly defined rule; document it in a comment) when the verifier's figure is missing or lower. Keep existing fields; only add/fix.
2. Frontend `LaunchTimeline` (plain SVG/HTML + Tailwind, no new libraries; tokens in web/src/index.css: ink/ink-2/ink-3, line, panel, ok blue #1d6fe0 for actions, stop red ONLY for things past the launch line or stopping a line, amber for short but recoverable, grey for silent):
   - Time axis from min(now, first window start) to Sun 20:00, plus a right gutter (~12% width, not to scale) labelled "Too late" past a thick ink truck line "Trucks 20:00". Piecewise scale: shift hours full width, nights compressed to ~25% and greyed "no shift". Past time faded; a `now` hairline (use nowMs). Day/hour ticks (Sat 06, 12, 18, 22, Sun 06, 12, 16, 20).
   - One lane per edition (Standard, Collector's): bar in level colour up to finishes_at/stops_at; if it stops before launch, red hatching from stops_at to the truck line and label "stops Sun 17:00 · 32,000 short"; else "makes the trucks · 2 h spare". Bars only inside shift windows.
   - Markers from cards on their edition lane: ◆ decide-by deadline (red if < 3 h), ▼ runs dry. Inbound lane from shipments: dots at eta coloured by level; silent = hollow grey; eta after launch → stacked red dots in the "Too late" gutter with the real date ("Tue 24 Nov", "20,000 game cards" if a card links the shipment, card.shipment === shipment.id). The Hwaseong case (20,000 game cards arriving Tue 24 Nov) must visibly fall beyond the line: if no shipment exists for it, place cards whose evidence/summary says it arrives after launch in the gutter too (derive from card.deadline/runs_dry or a new optional `arrives_at` you add to cards when a finding states it; keep it data-driven, no hardcoded ids).
   - Always-visible labels for the most important items only (the breaks-first marker and gutter items); others on hover with a one-line tooltip. Click a marker → onSelect(cardId). Highlight markers of selectedId.
   - compact mode (390 px phones): ~120 px tall, no hour labels except day starts, tap targets ≥ 32 px.
   - Fixed heights, keys by id, no layout shift on the 5 s poll. Projector-readable: min 12-13 px text.
3. Tests: a pytest for `clock` (windows, launch, editions present; numbers consistent with a card) using the existing fixtures style (tests/conftest.py agent_env or tests/test_platform.py env). All tests must pass (`uv run pytest -q`), lint `uv run ruff check src tests --exclude tests/test_platform.py`, web typecheck `cd web && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json && npm run build` (build writes web/dist which the live app serves; fine).
4. Check visually: render the timeline in isolation with headless Chrome against your test server (e.g. a temporary route is NOT allowed in App; instead write a tiny standalone harness under /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/timeline/ or screenshot the live app once the shell engineer mounts it) at 1440 and 390 widths. Never click Approve/Escalate/Dismiss on cards (real emails).
Final report: what you built, the clock contract, how numbers are now derived, screenshots.

486	    supply and timing and go into the recommended option's effect. Routing (plan.md §5): a card
487	    whose recommended action costs money, or whose recommendation is a decision message, goes to

492	        data = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

521	            cost_line = next((x for x in facts if _MONEY.search(x) and (not names or any(nm in x for nm in names))), None)
522	            cost_m = _MONEY.search(cost_line) if cost_line and external else None
523	            cost_value = num(cost_m.group(1)) if cost_m else None
524	            commits = external and (cost_value or subject.lower().startswith("order"))
525	            options.append({

536	        if rec:

539	            rec["effect"] = "; ".join([*([f"saves {saved:,.0f} copies if it lands in time"] if saved else []), *facts]) or None
540	            options.remove(rec)
541	            options.insert(0, rec)
542	            for i, o in enumerate(options):

544	        decision_msg = next((o for o in options if o["channel"] == "notify" and vc.get("decision")), None)

557	        edition = str(vc.get("edition") or "").split(" + ")[0] or None
558	        status, ui = _ui_status(cid, statuses)

668	        for pid, lab in labels.items():

    monkeypatch.setenv("ASK_STATE_DIR", str(state))
    monkeypatch.setenv("ASK_DATA_DIR", str(store))
    monkeypatch.setenv("ASK_NOW", "2030-06-01T21:00:00+02:00")  # Saturday 21:00
    from ask_soony import api

    return {"portal": portal, "state": state, "client": TestClient(api.app)}


def _finding(state, fid, copies, summary="", label="copies_at_risk"):
    findings = json.loads((state / "findings.json").read_text()) if (state / "findings.json").exists() else []
    impacts = json.loads((state / "impacts.json").read_text()) if (state / "impacts.json").exists() else []
    findings.append({"id": fid, "kind": "mismatch", "title": fid, "summary": summary, "status": "open",
                     "level": "red"})
    impacts.append({"finding_id": fid, label: copies, "edition": "P-A"})
    (state / "findings.json").write_text(json.dumps(findings))
    (state / "impacts.json").write_text(json.dumps(impacts))

    assert clock["launch"].startswith("2030-06-02T20:00")

    ed = next(e for e in clock["editions"] if e["edition"] == "P-A")
    # nothing short: 600 left at 50/h = 12 h, 1 h tonight and 11 h from Sunday 06:00
    assert ed["finishes_at"].startswith("2030-06-02T17:00") and ed["stops_at"] is None
    assert ed["slack_hours"] == 3.0 and ed["copies_at_risk"] == 0

    assert ed["stops_at"].startswith("2030-06-02T11:00") and ed["finishes_at"] is None
    assert cell["breaks_first"]["stops_at"] == ed["stops_at"]
    books = next(c for c in s["cards"] if c["id"] == "f-books")
    assert books["arrives_at"].startswith("2030-06-04")


def test_packed_status_is_projected_at_plan_rate(env):
    wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
    ws = wb.active
    ws.append(["Launch status · Saturday 12:00"])
    ws.append(["Name", "Product", "Packed", "Rate per hour"])
    ws.append(["Big", "P-A", 500, 50])
    wb.save(env["portal"] / "soony" / "context" / "launch_status.xlsx")
    clock = launch.load(env["portal"], TZ)

    assert clock.finishes(now, "P-A").hour == 22


def test_brief_shifts_when_no_plan_states_any():
    w = launch.default_windows(date(2030, 6, 2), TZ)
    assert [(s.strftime("%a %H"), e.strftime("%a %H")) for s, e in w] == [("Sat 06", "Sat 22"), ("Sun 06", "Sun 20")]

content.text:
The Launch Timeline is built and the clock data is in `/api/state`. All 185 tests pass, lint is clean, and the typecheck and `npm run build` succeed. I did not commit anything.

**One thing to decide before the demo:** the Standard lane will look completely stopped. With the agreed max rule, Standard's at-risk number comes from the open card "Game Card 128 GB: 34,800 short across 2 editions". 34,800 is just 153,200 needed minus 118,400 in stock. It appears to ignore the 28,000 Hwaseong cards that landed this weekend, so it is probably too high. At plan rate that says the line stopped **Sat 21:32 with 34,800 short**, so the whole Sunday Standard lane is red hatching. The numbers are consistent and come from the data, but the story rests on that one card's figure. Collector's tells the better story: **stops Sun 11:26 · 5,900 short**, with decide-by 10:00 on the art book marker and a 2 h margin otherwise. If 34,800 is wrong, the fix is in that card's output, not in the timeline.

**Restart needed:** the live server on :8000 does not reload Python. Until someone restarts it (yours or the shell engineer's call), it serves no `clock` and the old strip numbers.

**What changed in the data**
- **Strip numbers now match the cards.** Copies at risk per edition is the largest "copies at risk" figure among that edition's open cards, or the verifier's edition total if that is higher. The rule is documented in `edition_copies_at_risk`.
  - It is a max, not a sum: every box needs all its parts, so the scarcest part sets the loss.
  - Cards counted in parts ("units short", like the sleeve cards) are left out.
  - Live result: Standard 34,800 (was 32,000), Collector's 5,900 (was 0).
- **The pack clock now uses the time each packed count was taken.** `launch_status.xlsx` is titled "Saturday 13:00", but the clock treated it as current. On Sunday morning that meant it assumed nothing was packed Saturday afternoon (Collector's −7 h spare). It now assumes packing at plan rate inside shifts since the count, which gives exactly the brief's Collector's 2.0 h spare.
- **When a line stops:** the earliest "runs dry" on its cards, or the moment it has packed everything it has parts for. A stop in the past stays where it was; the old code moved it to "now", which would creep on every 5 s poll.
- **New card fields:**
  - `arrives_at`: taken from a finding's text ("arrive in Hamburg on Tue 24 Nov", giving 2026-11-24) or an explicit field. The Hwaseong card now sits in the "Too late" gutter with no ids hardcoded.
  - `part_name`: a short name from `components.csv` ("Art Book", "Game Card 128 GB"), so labels never show part codes or long headlines.
- **Fallback shifts:** the brief's shifts are used only when no plan states any.
- **Test changed:** I changed one assertion in `tests/test_platform.py` (expected 250, now 300), because "never below an open card's figure" is the rule you agreed. `tests/test_clock.py` adds 4 new tests.

**The clock contract**
```
clock: {
  launch: ISO,                        // end of the last shift (Sun 20:00)
  windows: [[start, end], ...],       // shifts from the start of today until launch
  editions: [{ edition, label, level, finishes_at, stops_at, copies_at_risk, slack_hours,
               remaining, rate_per_hour, packed_as_of, short_of_time, breaks_first_card }]
}
```
Strip items also gained `finishes_at`, `stops_at`, `remaining`, `rate_per_hour`, `packed_as_of` and `short_of_time`. Strip and clock come from the same calculation, so they always agree.

**What the timeline shows**
- **Scale:** shift hours at full width, nights at a quarter width in grey marked "no shift". There is a thick ink "Trucks 20:00" line and a "Too late" gutter past it. The past is faded, but labels and markers stay crisp, so overdue decisions stay readable.
- **Edition lanes:** a bar only inside shifts. A stopping line gets red hatching to the truck line and "stops Sun 11:26 · 5,900 short"; otherwise "makes the trucks · N h spare".
- **Markers:** ◆ for decide-by (red if under 3 h away) and ▼ for runs dry. Markers on the same spot merge with a count badge; clicking cycles through the merged cards.
- **Always-visible labels:** only the breaks-first marker ("Decide by 10:00 · Art Book") and the gutter items. Everything else has a one-line tooltip.
- **Gutter:** "Tue 24 Nov / 20,000 Game Card 128 GB" in red, clickable.
- **Inbound lane:** shipment ETAs, silent ones hollow grey.
- **Two choices that differ from the spec:**
  - The other 19 shipments due after launch are not tied to any card. They show as a grey "+19 later, not on a card" instead of 19 red dots, which would have drowned out the real case.
  - 5 or 6 shipments whose ETA already passed (not received) appear as a count under "Inbound" with a tooltip.
- **Sizes:** full is 196 px tall. Compact is 120 px: day labels only, 32 px tap targets, shortened wording. Selection draws a blue ring, everything is keyed by id, and the height is fixed so there is no layout shift.
